what_it_does: Neural rendering is a family of AI-assisted techniques that synthesize photorealistic images from learned 3D scene representations. Different methods — such as Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF, which casts rays through a learned volume) and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS, which represents a scene as millions of fuzzy blobs) — have very different computational profiles, so a chip optimized for one performs poorly on another. Uni-Render is a reconfigurable chip that identifies the computational building blocks common to multiple rendering pipelines (ray marching, blending many contributions along a ray, running small neural networks, and rasterizing Gaussian blobs) and builds a single hardware engine that can rearrange its data-movement pattern and operator assignments at runtime to match whichever algorithm is running. The goal is a single piece of silicon that efficiently handles the growing diversity of neural rendering approaches.
